title: COVID-19 (Temporary Measures for Solemnization and Registration of Marriages) Bill
what_it_is: COVID-19 (Temporary Measures for Solemnization and Registration of Marriages) Bill

sections.label: Video marriage solemnisations and registrations
sections.summary: The Bill would allow civil and Muslim marriages to be solemnised and registered via live video or television link during the COVID-19 period.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: If passed, it will allow marriage solemnisations and registrations for both civil marriages under the Women's Charter and Muslim marriages under the Administration of Muslim Law Act (AMLA), to be performed through a live video or live television link during the COVID-19 period.

sections.label: Extended marriage notice validity
sections.summary: Clause 2(2) extends marriage notice validity to 12 months from filing, including notices filed up to three months before the Act commenced.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Given the uncertainty over when the COVID-19 pandemic may end, clause 2(2) will allow couples to get married within 12 months from the date of filing their notice of marriage, instead of the current three months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: This means that marriage notices filed up to three months before the commencement of this Act, and which have not been cancelled or not expired, will automatically have their validity extended to 12 months.

sections.label: Video link marriage option
sections.summary: The Bill lets couples make statutory declarations and solemnise civil or Muslim marriages via live video link during the COVID-19 period.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The COVID-19 (Temporary Measures for Solemnization and Registration of Marriages) Bill will allow marriage solemnisations and registrations for both civil marriages under the Women's Charter and Muslim Marriages under the Administration of Muslim Law Act or AMLA, to be performed through a live video link during the COVID-19 period.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: This will give couples the option of making their statutory declarations and having their marriages solemnized via video link, if they prefer not to wait to do so in person.

sections.label: ROM and ROMM couple outreach
sections.summary: From 1 March to 30 April this year, ROM and ROMM reached out to about 3,500 couples.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: From 1 March to 30 April this year, ROM and ROMM have reached out to about 3,500 couples.

sections.label: Remote marriage solemnisation safeguards
sections.summary: Marriages may be solemnised remotely by video link, limited to couples with Singapore-issued documents and at least one Singaporean or Permanent Resident.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, now, during such unprecedented times, we have to adapt.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We are fortunate in being able to tap on technology to do so safely – by enabling marriages to be solemnised remotely through video links, without the need for couples to be present at the Registry of Marriages (ROM) or the Registry of Muslim Marriages (ROMM), or be in the physical presence of marriage solemnisers, religious leaders and witnesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While such an arrangement may have certain risks, I am confident that we are keeping these to a minimum by limiting this process to couples presenting Singapore-issued documents for verification and only allowing couples where at least one person is a Singaporean or Permanent Resident.

sections.label: Digital transfer of marriage documents
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether documents couples submit for marriage registration could be transferred digitally between Government agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Lastly, I would like to ask if certain documents which hopeful couples need to submit for the marriage registration could be transferred digitally between Government agencies.

sections.label: Specified period for Bill
sections.summary: Clause 2(6) and 3(5) define the specified period as when a control measure is in force or a further period prescribed by the Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The specified period for this Bill is defined in clause 2(6) and clause 3(5) as, one, “any period a control measure is in force”; or, two, “any further period that the Minister, having determined that it is necessary or expedient for the purposes of conducting any matter under this section in a safe and efficient manner and to prevent the spread of COVID-19, prescribes by order in the Gazette.” Although not required by statute, I hope the Minister will regularly review the situation and whether the need for the alternative arrangements under this Bill still persists or not.

sections.label: Cancellation of marriage notices
sections.summary: Clause 2(3) of the Bill seems to provide for a situation where a notice of marriage may be cancelled during the extended period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Children have brought us joy, even in difficult situations, such as those that we are facing now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: They are in relation to clause 2(3) of the Bill which seems to provide for a situation where a notice of marriage may be cancelled during the extended period.

sections.label: Retaining no-cancellation position
sections.summary: Another possibility is to retain that notices cannot be cancelled and apply the 12-month extension only to notices filed after commencement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Another possibility could be to retain the position that notices cannot be cancelled and, instead, only apply the time extension of 12 months to notices filed after the commencement of this Act.

sections.label: Virtual marriage solemnisation during circuit breaker
sections.summary: The Bill allows civil and Muslim marriages to be conducted virtually while COVID-19 circuit breaker and control measures are in place.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With the current circuit breaker measures in place, I understand that quite a number of marriage registrations and solemnisations have had to be postponed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, to allow Singaporeans to get married safely during this period, this Bill will allow marriage solemnisation and registrations for both civil marriages under the Women's Charter, and Muslim marriages under the Administration of Muslim Law Act, to be conducted virtually, while the COVID-19 circuit breaker and control measures are in place.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With the provisions made in this Bill, the above can be done virtually and through online means.

sections.label: Disruption to marriage plans
sections.summary: The question asks to what extent current circuit breaker measures have disrupted civil and Muslim marriage plans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Two, to what extent have the current circuit breaker measures in place disrupted marriage plans, both civil marriages and Muslim marriages?

sections.label: Muslim couples postponing solemnisation
sections.summary: Since 7 April, close to 200 Muslim couples postponed solemnisation and registration, and the Bill aims to give couples the option to continue using technology.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Since the start of the circuit breaker on 7 April, close to 200 Muslim couples have had to postpone their solemnisation and registration plans to reduce the risk of community transmissions of COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: With this Bill, the intention is to leverage available technology to give couples the option of continuing with their marriage solemnisation and registration, even as we continue to observe stringent social distancing measures.

sections.label: Mufti Irsyad on video link marriages
sections.summary: The Government consulted the Office of the Mufti, which issued an Irsyad stating video link arrangements will not affect a marriage's religious validity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The Government has consulted the Office of the Mufti, which has since issued an Irsyad stating that video link arrangements will not affect the validity of a marriage from a religious standpoint.

sections.label: Scheduled marriage solemnisations April to June 2020
sections.summary: Between 7 April and 1 June 2020, 2,723 marriage solemnisations were scheduled: 365 Muslim marriages and 2,358 civil marriages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Between 7 April and 1 June 2020, a total of 2,723 marriage solemnisations were originally scheduled: 365 of these were Muslim marriages and the remaining 2,358 were civil marriages.

sections.label: Extending notice of marriage validity
sections.summary: The validity of the notice of marriage is extended from three months to 12 months, and couples may apply to the Registrar to cancel it for valid reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: First, we are extending the validity of the notice of marriage from three months to 12 months to help couples who need to push back their wedding date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Second, we are also allowing couples to submit applications to the Registrar to cancel the notice of marriage if there are valid reasons to do so, such as the need to postpone their marriage till much later.
